one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: An integrated gold and silver platform in India serving businesses and consumers across 24 states as of March 31, 2026, spanning procurement and refining, bullion trading, digital gold offerings, jewellery manufacturing, international sales and facilitation of gold-backed financial services.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Augmont Enterprises operates two business verticals through distinct online platforms complemented by a physical distribution network: enterprise and international sales through the 'Augmont SPOT' electronic over-the-counter delivery-based bullion platform (operational since 2012, over 5,223 registered members as of March 31, 2026), and consumer-focused offerings through the 'Augmont Gold For All' platform launched in Fiscal 2021. Enterprise customers are jewellers, bullion dealers and manufacturers with valid GST registrations who buy gold and silver bars with assured physical delivery through 20 spot delivery centers across 13 states; the Company also sells gold bullion to asset management companies in exchange for gold ETF units and trades in gold and silver ETF units. It procures refined bullion from Indian and international banks, imports dore bars and scrap for refining at two units in Rudrapur (Uttarakhand) and Mumbai (Maharashtra), manufactures gold jewellery articles (primarily chains) for export at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur, and had served over 49.62 million registered digital gold consumers directly and through alliances as of March 31, 2026.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body:
The issuer describes itself as 'an integrated gold and silver platform in India serving businesses and consumers, with a presence across 24 states, as of March 31, 2026', whose 'operations span across multiple segments of the gold and silver value chain including procurement and refining, bullion trading, digital gold offerings, jewellery manufacturing, international sales and facilitating gold-backed financial services.'

BACKWARD INTEGRATION (upstream). Procurement runs through four disclosed channels: refined gold and silver bought from Indian and international banks; doré bars imported and refined in-house, which the RHP quantifies as carrying import duties 'lower ... by 0.65% as compared to directly importing refined gold'; scrap gold and silver bought from individuals, jewellers and at jewellery auctions 'at reduced rates'; and refined metal imported through the IIBX via the GIFT City subsidiary Augmont IFSC Private Limited, where the issuer 'execute[s] transactions directly as a trading member', saving 'expenses associated with brokerage and commission', and where 'the gold is procured from sources such as LBMA-accredited refiners or UAE Good Delivery-accredited refiners'. The issuer then owns the refining step itself, through two units (Rudrapur 144 MTPA and Mumbai 140 MTPA as of March 31, 2026) with in-house NABL/ISO-IEC-17025:2017-accredited assaying laboratories and BIS hallmarking licences, certified under India Good Delivery standards and authorised to deliver refined bullion on BSE- and MCX-operated commodity exchanges.

MANUFACTURING. A jewellery manufacturing unit at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur, Rajasthan (13.80 MTPA installed capacity as of March 31, 2026) converts metal into gold jewellery articles, primarily chains, for the international sales business.

FORWARD INTEGRATION (downstream). The issuer owns and operates both of its distribution platforms — 'Augmont SPOT' for enterprise customers (operational since 2012, 5,223 registered members) and 'Augmont Gold For All' for consumers (launched Fiscal 2021) — and owns the price-discovery layer on the enterprise side ('our pricing engine monitors these inputs through a combination of our in-house technology, AI powered tools and human oversight ... live tracking, predictive analysis and efficient hedging strategies'; 'we do not charge users of our platform any brokerage or terminal fees and we include our margins in the prices that are quoted on our platform'). Physical last-mile is partly owned and partly outsourced: of 20 spot delivery centres across 13 states, nine are operated directly and 11 through franchisees, with delivery 'typically fulfilled within two working days'.

WHERE INTEGRATION STOPS — THIRD-PARTY AND RELATED-PARTY DEPENDENCE. The consumer physical network is NOT owned: all 106 Gold-For-All centres are 'operated by Finkurve', a Group Company, and the issuer 'maintain[s] an asset light structure at these centers as they do not carry physical inventory'. Gold lending is not undertaken by the issuer at all — under a service level agreement dated June 1, 2024 (effective July 1, 2024) it only 'provide[s] technology, marketing and brand support through our platform for gold loans provided by' Finkurve. Consumer reach otherwise depends on third parties: 'over 218 partners such as Gullak, and Candere' for order placement, Kalyan Jewellers and CaratLane for physical redemption of digital gold, 3,700 Muthoot Fincorp branches for investment jewellery (a Technopak-sourced figure), an unnamed NBFC's stores, 705 independent financial agents, and third-party payment gateways for collections. The issuer states the synergy rationale itself: 'the gold and silver that we procure for selling on our 'Augmont SPOT' platform, helps us with our raw material requirements for manufacturing jewellery as well as for the other products and services that we provide through our consumer-focused business, thereby serving multiple business verticals', alongside centralised 'finance, information technology, strategy and procurement' functions.

STATED EXPANSION OF THE CHAIN. ₹ 4,650.00 million of the Net Proceeds is proposed to be used 'towards funding future working capital requirements towards procurement of raw material, maintenance of inventory and funding advance margin requirements for procurement purposes'; 15 new spot delivery centres are planned in Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities by Fiscal 2029; the issuer intends to fund 'minimum order quantity commitments under long-term supply arrangements our Company may enter with miners, in Fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029'; and it 'also propose[s] to expand our refining op' — the routed extract is cut off mid-sentence at that point, so the refining-expansion plan itself is NOT in the provided extract.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Prices of gold and silver and the ability to procure such materials - prices are set by LBMA benchmarks, international supply and demand, freight rates, the US Dollar volatility index, futures and options open positions, and domestic factors such as the domestic-international price disparity, bank premiums and taxes (Source: Technopak Report for the price-driver list)
- Procurement mix and cost structure - the majority of the cost structure is procurement; cost of materials consumed (dore bars and other unrefined metal) was ₹207,001.69 million, ₹189,480.77 million and ₹95,779.14 million, or 21.96%, 28.60% and 27.41% of total income, in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, while purchases of stock-in-trade (refined metal bought and resold) were ₹731,545.87 million, ₹468,497.85 million and ₹251,322.99 million, or 77.59%, 70.71% and 71.91% of total income
- Dore import arbitrage - imported dore bars carry duties lower by 0.65% than directly importing refined gold, so the refine-versus-buy decision is an explicit margin lever and directly drives capacity utilisation ('our capacity utilisation is directly related to our strategy of choosing between refining or purchasing pure bars')
- Volume of products sold - the key driver of revenue growth; optimum capacity utilisation at refining and manufacturing units is required to maximise profits, and there are no long-term agreements with customers, so production volumes may differ from estimates and results have fluctuated quarter to quarter
- Distribution network reach - 20 spot delivery centers across 13 states, 106 Finkurve-operated Gold-For-All centers, 705 independent financial agents and over 218 platform partners; most consumer-vertical arrangements are non-exclusive and terminable at counterparty discretion
- Government regulations and policies - approvals and licences from DGFT, BIS, GST authorities, municipal bodies, customs and securities market regulators, plus environmental, health, safety and labour laws at refining and manufacturing units, and exposure to geopolitical tensions and tariffs
- Working capital intensity - the business is working-capital intensive because funds are required to purchase gold and silver, and RBI circulars restrict access to bank debt financing for such requirements; total borrowings were only ₹126.72 million at March 31, 2026 with debt to equity of 0.01 times
- Hedging - the Company operates majorly on a hedged and back-to-back basis and does not take directional exposure to metal prices, utilising margin funds held by it to furnish margin requirements with recognised commodity exchanges and banks; Net Proceeds earmarked for working capital are not intended to be used for hedging margin

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expansion of enterprise and international sales - increase the number of customers to whom gold and silver bullion is sold, particularly in Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities, funded by Net Proceeds applied to working capital
- Expand the delivery network from 20 spot delivery centers across 13 states by setting up 15 new physical delivery centers across Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities by Fiscal 2029, each fully integrated with the Company's technology and logistics infrastructure
- Introduce additional products on the 'Augmont SPOT' platform such as hallmarked, quality-assured finished and semi-finished jewellery and copper-based and silver-based alloys, plus value-added services (market information reports, third-party finance and insurance options, hallmark unique identification verification)
- Sell international jewellery products to traders in additional international geographies beyond Hong Kong, Turkey and the UAE
- Facilitate the sale of lab grown diamonds on the 'Augmont SPOT' platform (trading facilitated from Fiscal 2026), using AI and machine learning enabled pricing tools and stone search
- Scale the consumer business through the 'Augmont Gold For All' platform, continuing to invest in the platform and introduce artificial intelligence and machine learning tools for customer insight and data analytics
- Work with Group Company Finkurve to open new Gold-For-All centers in underserved Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets on an asset-light basis (no physical inventory carried at the centers)
- Engage additional independent financial agents beyond the 705 onboarded as of March 31, 2026 to increase sales of products such as digital gold
- Strengthen procurement, refining and manufacturing operations - diversify and scale sourcing channels, increase dore bar volumes to negotiate better pricing terms, and deploy Net Proceeds towards strengthening bullion inventory levels including funding minimum order quantity commitments under long-term supply arrangements the Company may enter with miners in Fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029
- Expand refining operations at the existing Rudrapur and Mumbai units while investing in advanced refining technology to improve recovery rates, reduce turnaround times and scale volumes in line with market demand
- Grow jewellery manufacturing operations at Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur and expand exports to high-demand international markets

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The expansion narrative is network- and throughput-led rather than greenfield. On distribution, the Company intends to grow its enterprise delivery footprint from 20 spot delivery centers across 13 states (nine own, 11 franchisee-operated) as of March 31, 2026 by setting up 15 new physical delivery centers across Tier 3 and Tier 4 cities in India by Fiscal 2029, each integrated with its technology and logistics infrastructure, to shorten delivery timelines, onboard more jewellers in those regions and widen regional presence. On consumer reach, it intends to work with Group Company Finkurve to open new Gold-For-All centers (106 as of March 31, 2026) in underserved Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets on an asset-light basis, since those centers carry no physical inventory and are connected to the central platform and logistics network, and to engage additional independent financial agents beyond the 705 onboarded as of March 31, 2026. On production, rather than building new plants it proposes to expand refining at its existing Rudrapur (144 MTPA installed, 0.93% utilisation in Fiscal 2026) and Mumbai (140 MTPA installed, 8.53% utilisation in Fiscal 2026) units while investing in advanced refining technology to improve recovery rates, reduce turnaround times and scale volumes in line with market demand, and to grow jewellery manufacturing at the Sitapur SEZ, Jaipur unit (13.80 MTPA installed, 47.07% utilisation in Fiscal 2026) to serve additional international geographies beyond Hong Kong, Turkey and the UAE. Product-line expansion covers hallmarked finished and semi-finished jewellery and copper- and silver-based alloys on 'Augmont SPOT', value-added services, and lab grown diamond trading facilitated on the platform from Fiscal 2026. The RHP does not state a rupee capital expenditure amount for any of this - the Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for working capital and general corporate purposes, not capex.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep domain knowledge of the gold and silver industry with an integrated model spanning procurement and refining, bullion trading, digital gold, jewellery manufacturing, international sales and gold-backed financial services, and a well-established brand
- Diversified business model with synergies in operations
- Efficient procurement operations and a wide distribution network - procurement from Indian and international banks, imported dore bars (0.65% lower import duty than directly importing refined gold), and scrap from individuals, jewellers and auctions; domestic procurement was 81.83% and international 18.17% of total materials procured in Fiscal 2026
- Scalable technology enabled ecosystem with a robust price discovery mechanism - the 'Augmont SPOT' platform integrates live market data with proprietary algorithms to provide real-time bullion prices that typically update every second
- Track record of improved profit after tax from ₹759.66 million in Fiscal 2024 to ₹3,483.00 million in Fiscal 2026; revenue from operations grew from ₹349,214.93 million in Fiscal 2024 to ₹941,862.12 million in Fiscal 2026 at a CAGR of 64.23% and profit for the year at a CAGR of 114.12% (both CAGRs as stated in the RHP)
- Experienced Promoter and senior management team, helmed by Promoter and Whole-time Director Ketan Bhawarlal Kothari with over 13 years at the Company
- One of the few companies in India with a presence across both online and offline channels for the purchase of gold and silver, and one of the few refiners authorised to deliver refined bullion on BSE- and MCX-operated commodity exchanges (Source: Technopak Report)
- Recognised as India's 'Number 1 Gold Platform of the year 2024-2025' by the India Gold Conference, plus IBJA and India Silver Conference awards (Source: Technopak Report)
- High entry barriers in the businesses in which the Company operates - high working capital, multiple licences and permits, technology intensity, stringent quality management and effective price discovery capabilities (Source: Technopak Report)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Structurally thin operating margins on very large gross revenue, with revenue directly linked to metal prices — EBITDA margin was 0.41%, 0.46% and 0.30% and profit for the year margin 0.37%, 0.34% and 0.22% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 on revenue from operations of ₹941,862.12 million, ₹662,307.79 million and ₹349,214.93 million. The RHP states that given thin operating margins, even limited disruptions in hedging effectiveness, execution timing, liquidity conditions or counterparty performance during a sharp price correction may have a disproportionate adverse effect on EBITDA, profitability, net worth and cash flows, and that a decline in gold or silver prices reduces reported revenues one-for-one.
- Working-capital intensity combined with an inability to access bank debt financing — Operations require high working capital because funds are needed to purchase gold and silver, which are expensive commodities. RBI circulars and directions restrict the Company's access to debt financing for working capital; total borrowings were only ₹126.72 million with debt to equity of 0.01 times at March 31, 2026, and ₹4,650.00 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for working capital. Inability to access adequate and cost-effective funding in a timely manner would adversely affect operations, liquidity and financial performance.
- Severe and worsening customer concentration, with the largest customer being a Promoter Group entity — The top 10 customers accounted for 52.09%, 35.72% and 36.63% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the top 5 for 46.32%, 28.89% and 29.43%; and the largest single customer for 27.44%, 11.90% and 12.17%. The largest customer in Fiscals 2026 and 2025 was Riddisiddhi Bullions Limited, a Promoter Group member and Group Company (₹258,474.29 million in Fiscal 2026). No long-term agreements are executed with any customer.
- Extensive related-party dependence and potential conflicts of interest — The absolute sum of all related party transactions was ₹457,141.31 million, ₹244,390.98 million and ₹95,216.21 million in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; related party income items alone were 27.27%, 11.95% and 8.80% of revenue from operations. The consumer gold-loan proposition depends on a service level agreement with Group Company Finkurve, which also operates all 106 Gold-For-All centers.
- Revenue concentration in a single platform and a single business vertical — 'Augmont SPOT' generated 86.80%, 83.56% and 91.17% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and the business activity falls under one reported segment, gold refining and trading. The Company primarily conducts business through two self-owned online platforms, so any significant disruption in IT systems or breach of data security would directly affect revenue and reputation.
- Chronic under-utilisation of refining capacity — Capacity utilisation was 0.93% at Rudrapur (144 MTPA installed) and 8.53% at Mumbai (140 MTPA installed) in Fiscal 2026, with Rudrapur utilisation having fallen from 8.58% in Fiscal 2024. The RHP flags under-utilisation of manufacturing and refining facilities as a risk factor, while noting that utilisation is directly related to the strategy of choosing between refining and purchasing pure bars.
- Dependence on procurement continuity and on the imported dore bar duty differential — Business depends on continuous and cost-effective procurement of gold and silver, subject to global commodity price volatility, foreign exchange movements, changes in import duties and tariffs, evolving bullion-trade regulation, geopolitical tensions, sanctions and export controls affecting bullion-exporting countries. The economics of refining rest on a 0.65% lower import duty on dore bars versus refined gold, a policy-set spread outside the Company's control.
- Regulatory intensity, hedging and operational-integrity exposure across a licence-heavy gold value chain — Operations require numerous approvals from DGFT, BIS, GST authorities, customs and securities market regulators; the digital gold business of Material Subsidiary Augmont Goldtech Private Limited operates in an unregulated space; hedging is exposed to counterparty and exchange systemic risk; and the Company is exposed to theft and fraud, hazardous refining and manufacturing processes, and government measures or public appeals discouraging gold purchases.
